description: Verifies the covariance machinery and the variational geodesic integrator: covariance algebra and eigensystem, block extraction and Gaussian sampling, the flat-space Jacobian, the exact analytic covariance of a free particle, million-particle Monte-Carlo validation in Minkowski, Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes within 0.1 percent, and process noise injection.

checks.label: the first standard deviation is the root of the first variance
the second standard deviation is the root of the second variance
the eigenvalues of a covariance matrix are positive
the eigenvalues sum to the trace
the principal semi-axes are sorted in decreasing order
the squared semi-axes sum to the trace
the propagated variances stay positive
the confidence hypervolume is positive
the position block carries the expected variances and correlation
the spatial block carries the expected variances
the momentum block carries the expected variances and correlation
a multivariate Gaussian sample has eight components
the flat-space Jacobian has the identity in the position-momentum block and zeros elsewhere
the nominal worldline follows the straight-line solution
the propagated covariance equals the exact Sigma_xx = S0 + lambda^2 Sp, Sigma_xp = lambda Sp, Sigma_pp = Sp
the flat-space transition matrix has unit determinant
Minkowski: the semi-axes of the propagated covariance agree with the million-particle ensemble within the tolerance
Minkowski: the largest relative semi-axis error is below 0.1 percent
the transition matrix of a Hamiltonian flow has unit determinant
Schwarzschild: the semi-axes of the propagated covariance agree with the million-particle ensemble within the tolerance
Schwarzschild: the largest relative semi-axis error is below 0.1 percent
Kerr: the semi-axes of the propagated covariance agree with the million-particle ensemble within the tolerance
Kerr: the largest relative semi-axis error is below 0.1 percent
diffusion noise creates a positive variance in every phase-space direction
